title: Real-time dither engine
description: Turn a camera frame into a dithered image that uses only the colours of a chosen retro palette, using the real published ordered (Bayer) and error-diffusion algorithms, fast enough to run live.

clauses.text: Whatever algorithm and palette is chosen, every pixel of the result is one of the palette's colours - nothing in between.
clauses.observable_by: a test named "output uses only palette colours" passes for every algorithm

clauses.text: Ordered dithering uses the real Bayer threshold matrices, so a flat 50% grey becomes an exact half-on, half-off pattern.
clauses.observable_by: tests named "bayer matrices match the published values" and "bayer4 half grey is half white" pass

clauses.text: Error diffusion uses the published kernels (Floyd-Steinberg, Atkinson, Jarvis-Judice-Ninke, Stucki, Sierra), so tones are preserved on average - except Atkinson, which deliberately throws away a quarter of the error and so loses faint highlights and shadows like the original Mac did.
clauses.observable_by: tests named "error diffusion preserves average tone" and "atkinson drops faint tones" pass

clauses.text: Edge inputs never crash and never produce colours outside the palette: tiny or empty images, pure black and pure white.
clauses.observable_by: a test named "degenerate inputs are safe" passes

cases.description: random noise image through every algorithm x several palettes
2x2, 4x4 and 8x8 index matrices equal the recursive Bayer definition
flat grey 128 on a 1-bit palette gives exactly 8 of every 16 pixels white
flat 30% grey through FS, JJN, Stucki, Sierra gives 30% white within 2%
flat 10% grey: Atkinson yields no white pixels while Floyd-Steinberg yields about 10%
0x0, 1x1, pure black and pure white frames
every diffusion kernel matches an independent textbook implementation built from the published weights in RESEARCH 3.2 (catches swapped or wrong weights that average tone cannot)
for each level k/16, exactly the cells with index >= 16-k turn white (pins the (M+0.5)/n^2-0.5 rule and the spread)
at every one of the 16 cells, values just below and at r0, r1, r2 land on the right shade (the real 48-byte matrix)
